task_completion.description: Open the multi-species FASTA file in UGENE and identify the human sequence (P99999).
task_completion.visual_evidence: UGENE interface showing 'cytochrome_c_multispecies.fasta' open with multiple sequences listed, including Accession P99999.

task_completion.description: Isolate the human sequence and save it as a separate FASTA file.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A new tab or window in UGENE showing only the human Cytochrome C sequence, or a file explorer view showing 'human_cytc.fasta' created in the results directory.

task_completion.description: Execute the GOR IV secondary structure prediction on the human sequence.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GOR IV dialog box open in UGENE, or the 'Secondary Structure' annotation track appearing below the human sequence in the sequence view.

task_completion.description: Export the predicted secondary structure annotations to a GFF/GFF3 file.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Export' or 'Save' dialog showing the file format set to GFF/GFF3 and the destination path 'cytc_secondary_structure.gff'.

task_completion.description: Identify and export the longest alpha-helix sequence to a FASTA file.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Selection of a specific region of the sequence (the longest helix) and the creation of 'longest_helix.fasta' in the file system.

task_completion.description: Create a text report with the required structural statistics and coordinates.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A text editor or terminal view showing 'structure_summary.txt' with counts for helices/sheets and specific coordinates for the longest helix.

integrity.description: The agent used the UGENE GUI for bioinformatics tasks rather than command-line tools like 'grep' or 'sed' to manipulate the FASTA.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show mouse cursor movement, menu selections, and UGENE dialog boxes rather than just terminal commands.

integrity.description: The secondary structure data was generated by the UGENE GOR IV plugin, not manually typed.
integrity.visual_evidence: The presence of the UGENE 'Secondary Structure' track with H (helix), E (strand), and C (coil) labels visible in the GUI.

integrity.description: The agent saved files to the specific paths requested in the instructions.
integrity.visual_evidence: Save dialogs or file explorer views showing the full path: ~/UGENE_Data/results/cytc_structure/.

privileged_info_for_vlm: Human Cytochrome C (P99999) is 105 amino acids long. Using GOR IV, the longest alpha-helix typically spans residues 92-103 (length 12, sequence: ERADLIAYLKKA) or a similar region near the C-terminus. There are usually 3-5 alpha-helices and 0-2 beta-strands predicted depending on the specific GOR IV implementation/parameters in UGENE. The VLM should verify that the coordinates in the summary report match the visual annotations in the UGENE sequence view.
